title: Why Brand New Ships Are Already Covered in Rust

scenes.text: Look at almost any working ship and you will see rust running down the sides.
Even on vessels that left the shipyard only months ago.
It looks like neglect. Like nobody has maintained it in years.
But most of that rust is not the hull at all.
A ship is covered in bolts, railings, hatches and fittings, all different metals.
Salt water collects in every joint and seam, and it never fully dries.
Those small parts corrode first, long before the steel around them.
Rain then carries the stain downward, painting streaks across good paint.
At sea, a spotless hull does not mean a healthy ship. It means a recent repaint.
